decisions.evidence: The fixed-endpoint rational path construction and real Stone–Weierstrass followed by rational coefficient approximation close the reader’s two proof gaps. Current item retains the reader proof; the contract was enriched with its completed risk review after the post-reader snapshot. Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, Ch. 11, supports regular boundary use.

The same barrier multiple bounds both deviations on the compact boundary complement, with its empty case explicit; the lower and upper Perron inequalities now follow. Checked against Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Theorem 11.7, pp. 228–229. Contract risk review changes the post-reader carrier.

For E equal to the full circle and z=c, integrating the periodic kernel over all real t would give infinite mass. The Statement and measure construction now restrict t to [0,2pi), matching proof 1.2 and yielding probability one. The direct arc consumer uses this exact range.

The repaired proof now establishes the lambda-system closure under increasing unions and uses the declared pi-lambda theorem for all Borel sets; the previous finite-union inference was insufficient. Contract risk review changes the post-reader carrier.

The false involution assertion is absent. The disc automorphism computation and uniform boundary decay on circles |a|<r<1 justify the Green candidate and leastness. Contract risk review changes the post-reader carrier.

The proof correctly uses w-beta nonzero off the pole, including points with zero real part of that difference. The half-plane maximum comparison and square-root pullback retain the claim. Contract risk review changes the post-reader carrier.

The kernel and return-word count use j=1,...,d and exactly 2d neighbours. The balanced-multinomial/Stirling estimate gives O(n^-d/2), summable for d>=3, as in Durrett §5.4 with the authored all-d extension. Contract risk review changes the post-reader carrier.

The normalized denominator Q has degree d>=1 and needs a root before step 4.1 can form nonempty zero neighbourhoods. Added the exact published FTA statement, dependency, contract citation and manifest dependency; coprimality then separates the zero sets.

The reader’s radial interpolation reaches radius one half for every nonzero starting point and stays in the punctured disc. I also corrected a separate refuter finding at verification 4.1; the current item differs from both scope snapshots.

At xi=i and a=(1+i)/4 the former middle modulus |xi-conj(a)| differed from |xi-a|. The corrected identity |1-conj(a)xi|=|conj(xi)-conj(a)|=|xi-a| uses |xi|=1 and conjugation and establishes the required boundary datum.

A nonconstant entire function has a nonempty set of positive Taylor indices with nonzero coefficient. The least index now invokes the published well-ordering principle for N, declared in the item, contract and manifest.
Unbounded finite-disc pole counts give a nonempty set of integer threshold radii. Step 2.1 now invokes the published well-ordering principle for N, declared in the item, contract and manifest.

The reader corrected the page’s inaccurate well-ordering-of-integers summary to natural numbers, matching the published theorem. The page file and page-level manifest metadata still match the post-reader carrier; the later item dependency edits do not change this page carrier.

The high-risk review found that verification 1.1's preimage statement was false for shifted arcs crossing the period boundary. The current proof reduces the interval modulo 2π, splits at 2π when needed, and uses periodicity with endpoint sets ignored. The item hash differs from both Step-5 snapshots; this records the repaired finding without treating the unchanged reader carrier as an accepted repair.

The critical risk review found that the barrier proof claimed a maximum on an empty boundary complement when a neighbourhood contains the whole boundary. The current proof separates that vacuous case from the nonempty compact complement case. Its item hash differs from the Step-5 snapshots, and the statement change remains separately adjudicated under refuter:26:2.
